title: Why 4K Video Loads Faster Than a 2 MB Email Attachment 🤯 #shorts
description:
Streaming video and email attachments travel very differently. YouTube splits a video into small chunks, serves them from a server close to you (often inside your internet provider), and starts playing after the first few seconds while the rest keeps downloading. An email attachment is re-encoded as text (Base64), which makes it about a third bigger, and it hops through several mail servers that each store and scan it. You can't open it until the whole message has arrived.

📘 More to learn + my projects: https://github.com/HemashreeVI

#YouTube #Email #Internet #Streaming #Tech #TechExplained #shorts

lines: A 4K video starts playing in a second. A 2 MB email attachment takes its time.
YouTube doesn't send you the whole video. It sends small chunks, and starts playing after the first few seconds.
And those chunks come from a server near you, often right inside your internet provider.
Your attachment takes a longer road. It's re-encoded as text, about a third bigger, and hops through mail servers that each store and scan it.
And you can't open any of it until the whole thing has arrived.
Video streams in pieces. Email arrives all at once.
